title: Minimum-cost worker schedule
prompt_text: A nightly job must process 4,320 records within 120 minutes. Two workers are available. Worker A processes 24 records per minute and costs 3 credits per minute while running. Worker B processes 40 records per minute and costs 6 credits per minute while running. Both can run at the same time, each can be started and stopped at any whole minute, and records can be split between them in any way. Find the schedule that minimises total credits, and state the minimum cost. Show the reasoning.

content:
**Minimum total cost: 576 credits**

Reasoning:

- Worker A processes 24 records/min at a cost of 3 credits/min, so its cost per record is  
  \[
  \frac{3}{24}=0.125\text{ credits/record}
  \]
- Worker B processes 40 records/min at a cost of 6 credits/min, so its cost per record is  
  \[
  \frac{6}{40}=0.15\text{ credits/record}
  \]
  Thus Worker A is cheaper per record.

Worker A alone can process only  
\[
24 \times 120 = 2880
\]
records in 120 minutes, which is less than 4320. Therefore Worker A should run for the full 120 minutes.

Remaining records:  
\[
4320 - 2880 = 1440
\]
Worker B processes 40 records/min, so time needed:  
\[
\frac{1440}{40}=36\text{ minutes}
\]

Total cost:  
\[
(3 \times 120) + (6 \times 36)
= 360 + 216
= 576\text{ credits}
\]

**Optimal schedule:**  
- Worker A runs all 120 minutes.  
- Worker B runs 36 minutes.  

**Minimum total credits: \(\boxed{576}\)**
